hypothesis: PySnooper's get_source_from_frame decodes source files using the locale-dependent default encoding when no PEP-263 coding declaration is present, so a UTF-8 source file containing non-ASCII characters is mis-decoded (mojibake) under a non-UTF-8 locale, corrupting the traced source line.
trigger: Create a temporary module file encoded as UTF-8 whose function body contains a non-ASCII string literal (e.g. 'héllo') and no coding declaration; import it, decorate the function with pysnooper.snoop(string_io), and run it under a non-UTF-8 locale (LC_ALL=C).

oracle.expected_behavior: The trace output must contain the exact non-ASCII source line text (e.g. the literal 'héllo') as written in the UTF-8 file, independent of the process locale.
oracle.target_evidence: pysnooper/tracer.py get_source_from_frame: when source is bytes it sets encoding='ascii' and only overrides it if a PEP-263 coding declaration is found in the first two lines; otherwise it decodes with that encoding. The README and tests (e.g. test_unavailable_source, test_string_io) show source lines are echoed verbatim into trace output, so a mis-decoded line is a functional defect.
oracle.historical_evidence: cookiecutter:1 shows the same class of locale-dependent implicit text decoding bug (UTF-8 data read with platform default encoding); PySnooper:3 is only weakly related (file-output path variable mismatch).
